Emily —

Thanks — understood. I put together a short operational playbook and attached a sample minimal manifest (sample_admin_manifest.jsonl) — the PDF explains the export modes and per-field retention. High level:

- What we log: authenticated console sessions (login, logout), operator actions (role grants, deploy, rollback, scale, revoke key), API admin calls (user, method, resource, args metadata), privilege escalation events, and operator console overrides. Each event includes: timestamp (UTC), actor (internal id + human name where available), actor_role, source_ip, session_id, target_resource, and op_details (action-specific fields).
- Retention: default tenant-scoped retention for admin events is 365 days. System-level debug traces may be 30 days. Customers on enterprise plans (Dedicated/Private) can request bespoke retention up to 7 years via contract.
- Exports: three modes — ad-hoc S3 export (signed presigned-put manifest), scheduled bulk export (parquet/jsonl bundles to a customer S3 or SFTP), and streaming subscription (Kafka/SQS via partner integration). All exports are tenant-scoped by default.
- Timestamps: we normalize to UTC at ingest; event ordering guarantees per-session (monotonic sequence numbers in the manifest); clock skew tolerance is +/- 5s in metadata and we include server-side monotonic counters for forensic ordering.
- Chain of custody: every bundle is delivered with a signed manifest (SHA256 checksums per file), GPG-signed manifest for Dedicated customers who request proof, and TLS + SSE-KMS encryption in transit/at-rest. We provide a manifest signing key thumbprint and an attestation statement when requested.
- Redaction & scoping: exports support column-level redaction (PII hash or suppression) and can be filtered to tenant_id, project_id, or time window. We do not redact operator ids by default — auditors usually prefer identifiable operator linkage.

I'm attaching the playbook PDF and the sample manifest. Kimberly, can you confirm whether we can include a short snippet of the signing key thumbprint and the current S3 export throughput limits? Karthik, can you add the ops runbook steps on how to trigger an ad-hoc export and the expected SLA (hours to hand off)?

Marcus
Director, Customer Security (on behalf of Redwood Inference)

Quick answers to the throughput / SLA items Emily asked for:

- Ad-hoc S3 export: typical manifest generation + bundle creation for a 30-day tenant window is 2–6 hours depending on volume; for large exports (>500GB) we coordinate a prioritized transfer which can be 24–72 hours.
- Scheduled bulk export: daily/weekly with incremental deltas — near-instant delivery to a pre-provisioned bucket (subject to network egress limits); we provide resumable multipart uploads.
- Streaming subscription: at ingest we can stream admin events at peak firehose rates compatible with standard Kafka (partitions/scaling applies). Customers that need a bounded replay window and attested sequence numbers use our signed manifest + replay index.

On signing keys: we publish a rotating manifest-signing keyset. For Dedicated customers we offer a customer-managed KMS option where the manifest is encrypted with a key the customer controls and we still add our signature for sequence attestation.

Emily — happy to hop on a quick 20-min call if the auditor has follow-ups; otherwise the attached playbook + manifest should hit the items they asked for.

Kimberly
Senior Product Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
